meta_description: All your agent-built projects, in one place.
projects_empty_body: Connect your code to import your projects, or start one from your conversation.
signin_body: Sign in with GitHub: that is where your repositories live. Pono keeps no password.
signin_none: No sign-in is configured on this server.
projects_connect_first: Connect your code and your hosts first.
connections_intro: Your own accounts, which Pono uses for you: your code, your hosts, your databases, visit counting. Start with the code; the rest comes when you need it.
error_connection_unreachable: The provider does not answer. Try again.
import_intro: Pick a repository: Pono finds its hosting, its database and its last deployment by itself.
error_project_already_imported: This repository is already in the workshop.
usage_intro: All your subscriptions and what your providers consume. Every figure says where it comes from.
usage_no_reading: No reading yet. Connect your providers, then read.
servers_intro: One server per project. Only awake servers count against your plan.
servers_none: No server. Launch a project, or give one to a project from its page.
servers_release_confirm: Release this server? Its disk is deleted; saved code stays in your repository.
limit_body: Pick a project to put to sleep: its disk is kept, it wakes on the next request.
catalog_intro: A ready solution for your case, or an empty project. Skills teach your agent to do it right.
launch_name_help: Lowercase, digits and dashes: it becomes the repository name.
launch_done: Ready in {seconds} s: repository, project and server.
agents_intro: An agent acts with your rights, never more. It never validates a release, never changes the mode, never rolls back.
agents_token_once: Copy this token now: it will never be shown again.
settings_billing_none: Billing is not configured on this server.
mode_ask_body: Nothing reaches production without your validation.
mode_auto_body: When the three guards pass, Pono merges by itself. A refusal stays a refusal.
mode_bypass_body: The agent ships alone; migrations and preview become warnings. A secret always blocks.
releases_rollback: Roll back to the previous version
releases_rollback_confirm: Roll back? The host puts the previous version back online; the database is not touched.
protection_unavailable_on_plan: protection unavailable on the GitHub plan of the repository
project_no_server: This project has no Pono server.
error_servers_limit_reached: Every awake server of your plan is taken.
error_launch_name_taken: A repository with that name exists.
error_release_changed: The proposal changed since it was evaluated: evaluate it again.
error_release_person_only: Only a person, in the console, decides this.
error_admin_forbidden: Reserved to the operators of the platform.
action_admin_server_slept: Server put to sleep by the operator
manifest_proposed_body: Pono pre-filled this project's pono.yaml in a pull request. Complete it and merge it: it becomes the truth Pono reads.
skills_rule: Skills guide the agent. Turning them off removes no guard: Pono still applies them. The repository's own conventions come first.
level_title: How do you want to work?
level_body: Your agents follow the same answer. You can change it any time in the settings.
level_guided_body: You describe what you need; Pono picks the technology and the template and launches the project.
level_choosing_body: Pono offers two or three templates and a few options; you choose.
level_expert_body: Your technology, your architecture, your skills. Pono keeps the frame: costs, server, release.
signin_why_github: Pono goes through GitHub: your account and your repositories are linked in one step, and your projects stay yours.
signin_no_github: No GitHub account yet? Create one (free)
catalog_own_skills_body: Your way of doing, kept for your agents. Private until you ask to share it; Pono reviews before anything is shared.
admin_catalog_import_body: The repository holds pono-template.yaml and its skills in .pono/skills/; it becomes the starter of the projects launched from it.
error_catalog_name_taken: That name is taken in the catalog.
error_catalog_unreadable: The repository does not read as a template (pono-template.yaml).
error_catalog_not_found: Nothing like that in your catalog.
visits_link: Link this project to a site
visits_connect: Connect Umami or PostHog to count visits
visits_gap_not_linked: This project is linked to no site.
visits_gap_not_connected: The analytics provider is not connected.
visits_gap_provider_refused: The analytics provider did not answer.
error_analytics_site_not_found: No such site at the provider.
authorize_body: This agent will see your projects, your usage and your servers, with the rights chosen below. You can cut this access any time in Agents.
authorize_never: No agent approves a release, changes the mode, rolls back, or sees a key.
variables_rule: Type each value here, once: it is sealed and goes to this project's server only, at its next start. Never a production key; an agent only sees the names.
error_variables_person_only: A value is set by a person, in the console.
error_variable_invalid_name: A name in CAPITALS, not starting with PONO_.
error_oauth_unknown_client: This client is not known to Pono.
error_rate_limited: Too many requests; try again shortly.
dev_push_refused: Push refused: a secret in {file}. Remove it, then push again.
dev_phase_crashed: stopped on an error (see the log)
error_dev_no_server: Give this project a server first.
error_dev_server_asleep: The server sleeps: wake it to develop.
error_dev_unknown: Nothing says how this project runs: add dev: (install, command, port) to pono.yaml.
error_dev_clone_failed: The repository could not be fetched on the server.
error_dev_pull_failed: The server could not take the changes (diverged history?).
error_dev_push_failed: The push was refused (not on dev, or behind).
top_search: Search a page or a project…
overview_intro: Your projects, their servers and what your subscriptions use. Every figure comes from the same data as the rest of Pono.
overview_calm: Your {count} projects are in their normal state.
overview_projects_foot: Sorted by last activity · state read from pono.yaml and the hosts
overview_servers_none: No server yet: give one to a project from its page.
overview_servers_foot: One server per launched project · plan limit: {limit}
overview_usage_foot: Read at each provider with your keys · warning at 80 %
next_server: Give a project a server for your agent to work on
next_template: Start a project from a template
next_foot: Your agent can do each of these for you
projects_intro: Every project your agents built, whatever the repository or the stack.
admin_intro: What happens across the platform: organizations, servers, revenue and catalog. Never people’s code, data or keys.
admin_ok: The wallet, the servers and the catalog are in order.
admin_wallet_low: The Agent37 wallet is nearly empty: {balance}.
admin_wallet_short: The Agent37 wallet does not cover the month: {balance} for {cost}.
admin_limit_full: Every active server slot of the account is taken: {active}/{limit}.
admin_wallet_foot: Read at Agent37 · pays for every organization’s servers
admin_privacy: Counts and states only: never code, data or keys
admin_servers_none: No server on the platform yet.
admin_catalog_empty: No template or skill imported yet.
agents_what: An agent is Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Codex, connected to Pono over MCP. Once connected, it sees your projects, codes on their server and proposes releases, with your rights, never more.
agents_how_1_body: Pick a name and what the agent may do. Pono creates a token, shown once.
agents_how_2_body: Into Claude Code or Codex. The Pono plugin adds the project’s context and the status line.
agents_how_3_body: The agent sees your projects, starts the preview, pushes to dev and proposes the release. You decide.
agents_cut_confirm: Cut the access of “{name}”? The agent will no longer reach Pono.
agents_scope_read_body: Sees projects, their state, servers and usage. Changes nothing.
agents_scope_act_body: Can also launch a project, start the preview, push to dev and propose a release.
agents_config_codex: In Codex (~/.codex/config.toml), with the token in PONO_TOKEN:
agents_can_body: The tools of Pono’s MCP server, by family. With “Read only”, only those that read answer.
agents_can_projects_body: Find the folder’s project, pick up where things stood, launch or adopt a project.
agents_can_dev_body: Start the preview on the project’s server, pull and push to dev after the secrets check.
agents_can_release_body: Propose a release and ask for a rollback. The decision stays yours.
agents_can_skills_body: Read the project’s guidance, write new skills, save a project as a template.
agents_can_servers_body: See servers, wake or sleep them, read what services use and the visits.
agents_can_variables_body: See variable names, ask for a value — that only you type — and read your level.
agents_never: An agent never approves a release, never changes the release rule, never rolls back and never sees a secret’s value.
catalog_templates_body: A template is a starting repository: the stack, pono.yaml and the skills. Pono creates your repository from it.
catalog_skills_body: A skill is written guidance for your agent. Each project picks its own in pono.yaml; the agent reads them at the start of every session.
catalog_own_none: No skill of your own yet.
catalog_own_foot: Your agent can write one too (create_skill) or save a project as a template
launch_what: Pono creates the repository, the project and its server; your agent can start right away
connections_ok: {count} services connected: your projects can be imported and followed.
connections_hint_hosting: Connect a host to follow releases.
connections_start: Connect your code: without GitHub, Pono sees no project.
connections_cut_confirm: Cut {name}? Pono deletes the key; what depends on it will no longer be followed.
connections_key_help: The key is checked at {name}, encrypted, then never shown again.
kind_why_code_host: Where your code lives. Pono reads your repositories there, creates new ones and opens release proposals.
kind_why_hosting: Where your sites run. Pono reads release states and usage there. One is enough.
kind_why_database: Your Postgres databases. Pono creates one per launched project and follows their usage.
kind_why_analytics: To count your sites’ visits, without cookies. Pono links each live project to its site.
kind_why_ai: Your AI key, if a project needs one. Pono only follows what it costs.
import_how_1_body: From your GitHub account. Nothing changes in the repository.
import_how_2_body: Its hosting, database, last deployment, and its pono.yaml if it has one.
import_how_3_body: With its state. You can then give it a server for your agent to work on.
servers_how_1_body: Your agent writes the code there, and the preview runs there with its address.
servers_how_2_body: After a while without activity. A sleeping server keeps its files and does not count in your plan.
servers_how_3_body: Only active servers count. At the limit, Pono asks which one to put to sleep.
settings_intro: How you work, your plan and your language.
settings_level_body: Pono and your agents adapt to your answer: what they offer, what they show first.
settings_level_foot: Your agents read this choice with get_profile
settings_plan_foot: Payment goes through Stripe; you can change plan at any time
settings_language_body: The console exists in French and English. Your choice is kept.
usage_calm: No service is above 80 % of its quota.
usage_sources_explained: Measured: read at the provider · estimated: computed by Pono · declared: typed by you
usage_meters_body: One card per service, its meters against their quota. The line marks the 80 % warning.
usage_subscriptions_body: What you pay monthly or yearly that Pono cannot read by itself: declare it to see everything in one place.
home_eyebrow: For coding from Claude or ChatGPT
home_title_2: Your agent gets a server for every project.
home_lede: Add Pono to Claude or ChatGPT, on your phone or your computer. Your agent writes the code on the project's server, you see the result live, and production obeys your rule. Nothing to install.
home_fine: Free for one active project · No card needed · Your code stays on your GitHub
home_preview_verdict: invoices-api stopped answering after the 2:02 pm merge.
home_preview_verdict_body: Pono offers to go back to the previous version: one click.
home_works_with: Works with what you already use
home_problem_title: Coding with an agent took a machine, a terminal, and watching everything yourself.
home_problem_body: Pono gives your agent a ready server for every project, and keeps the rest: where each project stands, what it costs, and releases under your rule.
home_f1_body: Last commit, last deploy, a production address that answers or not: the truth about each project, read again every 15 minutes.
home_f2_body: GitHub, Netlify, Cloudflare, Neon or OpenAI meters against their quotas, plus your subscriptions. An alert before you go over, not after.
home_f3_body: Your agent reads and edits the code there, runs commands, and you watch the preview change live. It sleeps on its own and never exceeds its budget.
home_f4_body: You choose the rule: approve by hand, or merge automatically when everything is green. If production breaks after a merge, Pono rolls back.
home_f5_body: Claude or ChatGPT, on the web or your phone; Claude Code or Codex if you prefer the terminal. One address to paste, you allow, it's connected.
home_f6_body: Start from a proven base: stack, security, design. Skills tell the agent how to work well, project by project.
home_how_title: Three steps, and your agent is at work.
home_step_1_body: One sign-in, and you choose which repositories Pono can see. Nothing changes on your side.
home_step_2_body: Paste Pono's address in Claude's or ChatGPT's connectors, and allow. No key to copy.
home_step_3_body: "Add a contact form": the agent codes on the server, you open the preview, then approve the release.
home_agents_title: One address to paste, and your chat codes your projects.
home_agents_body: Pono offers 41 MCP tools: resume a project, read and edit its code, run commands, see the preview, push to dev, propose a release.
home_agents_never: An agent never approves a production release, never changes your rule, and never sees a secret.
home_pricing_title: You pay for servers awake, nothing else.
home_pricing_body: Every plan has unlimited projects, meters, alerts and agent access.
home_plan_free_for: To try it, or run a single active project.
home_plan_solo_for: For anyone running several projects at once.
home_plan_pro_for: For a small team or a studio.
home_plan_pay: Month by month, by Mobile Money or card. Stop whenever you want.
home_a1: No. Your projects stay with your providers (Netlify, Cloudflare, Coolify…), on your accounts. Pono provides the server where your agent codes, and watches production.
home_a2: It stays in your GitHub repository. Pono copies it nowhere else, and only pushes to the dev branch, after a secrets check.
home_a3: Sealed apart, never shown, never given to an agent. Cut a connection whenever you want.
home_q4: I have no computer: can I still?
home_a4: Yes. Claude or ChatGPT on your phone is enough: the agent codes on the project's server, and you open the preview in your browser.
home_final_title: Your projects deserve better than a pile of tabs.
home_final_body: Connect GitHub, add Pono to your chat, and ask for your first change.
home_footer: The frame for every project your agents build.
start_title: Three steps, and your agent codes for you.
start_body: From Claude or ChatGPT, on your phone or your computer: nothing to install.
start_step_github_body: Pono sees the repositories you opened to it. Change them on GitHub whenever you want.
start_step_agent_body: Add Pono to your assistant: it sees your projects, codes on their server and proposes releases.
start_step_project_body: Import a repository, start from a template, or just ask your agent.
start_ask_text: With Pono, build a website for my business and show it to me.
connect_claude_1: Open Claude (web, desktop or phone): Settings, then Connectors.
connect_claude_2: "Add custom connector": name it Pono, and paste the address below.
connect_claude_3: Click Connect, then Allow on Pono's page. That's all.
connect_chatgpt_1: Open ChatGPT: Settings, then Apps & Connectors, then Advanced: turn on developer mode.
connect_chatgpt_2: "Create": name it Pono, paste the address below, OAuth authentication.
connect_chatgpt_3: Confirm, then Allow on Pono's page.
connect_code_1: In your terminal, add Pono to Claude Code:
connect_code_2: In Claude Code, type /mcp, pick pono, then Authenticate: your browser opens on Pono, you allow.
connect_codex_1: Codex connects with an access key: create it here, it shows only once.
connect_codex_2: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml, and the key in the PONO_TOKEN variable:
connect_try: Then tell it: "Show me my Pono projects".
agents_can_code_body: Read, search and edit the project's files and run commands on its server, with no machine of your own. The preview reloads.
connections_path_title: To take a project all the way online
connections_ready_all: Everything is ready to go all the way online.
connections_ready_code: You can code. To go online, connect a host.
connections_step_paste: Paste it here, Pono checks it right away.
connections_failed_now: Connecting {name} did not work. Try again, or use a key.
admin_top_up_hint: The payment opens at the server provider.
dev_preview_shared: A link to send, valid until {until}. It closes by itself after.
network_open_help: The server can reach the whole internet. Limit it so that a rigged package or a stray command cannot send your data elsewhere.
network_limited_help: The server reaches only the addresses below. A command that needs another one is refused, and your agent tells you which to add.
network_always: Always allowed: package registries, your code host and your connected services.
network_invalid: A domain is unreadable: write it like api.example.com or *.example.com.
network_not_enforced: The server host cannot limit the network: the choice is kept, not enforced.
backups_help: The whole server is backed up every night (7 days kept). Back up before a risky step; you can go back from here.
backups_none: No backup yet: the first comes tonight, or now with the button.
backups_restore_confirm: Put the server back as it was on {date}? Everything written since will be lost, and the dev server will stop. It takes a few minutes.
backups_restoring: Restoring: a few minutes. Start the dev server again after.
error_server_backup_too_soon: One backup on demand every 15 minutes: the last one is kept.
error_server_restoring: A restore is already under way.
project_online_done: The site is created and building: {url}. It will be live in a minute or two, then follow every merge to the main branch.
project_online_no_hosting: Connect a hosting (Netlify) in Connected services first: Pono will create the site there.
error_code_host_permission_missing: GitHub refuses to add the read key: the Pono app needs the “Administration” permission on this repository. Accept the permission update on GitHub, then try again.
error_hosting_name_taken: No free name was found at the hosting: try again.
